etymologies.etymologyHTML: From treat +‎ -ment. Compare French traitement.

definitions.definition: The process or manner of treating someone or something.
Medical care for an illness or injury.
The use of a substance or process to preserve or give particular properties to something.
(countable) A treatise; a formal written description or characterization of a subject.

quote.citation: 1992, Rudolf M[athias] Schuster, The Hepaticae and Anthocerotae of North America: East of the Hundredth Meridian, volume V, Chicago, Ill.: Field Museum of Natural History, →ISBN, page vii:
quote.text: Firstly, I continue to base most species treatments on personally collected material, rather than on herbarium plants.

definitions.definition: (countable, film) A brief, third-person, present-tense summary of a proposed film.

quote.citation: 1725–1726, Homer, “Book 14”, in [William Broome, Elijah Fenton, Alexander Pope], transl., The Odyssey of Homer. […], London:  […]  Bernard Lintot, →OCLC:
quote.text: Accept such treatment as a swain affords.
